newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks revive on industrial production data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks revive on industrial production data.

text.p: Mexican stocks resumed their initial upward trend in late morning trade on Thursday in the wake of stronger-then-expected industrial production figures, dealers said.
"The production figures were very good and kick-started the bourse amid a session that was otherwise quiet," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 23.34 points, or 0.47 percent, at 5,039.97.
The Financial Ministry announced Mexico's industrial production in June rose by 9.9 percent in year-ago terms. A previously conducted Reuters survey had forecast an average increase of 8.3 percent.
Dealers said the bourse had begun to pare initial gains on the back of the Dow Jones before the data were released.
Trading volume was slow at 29.4 million shares
On the broad market, gains outnumbered declines by 46 to 18, out of 85 stocks traded in total.
Volume was far thinner than for many recent sessions at 55.9 million shares traded.
The Dow Jones was down 53.42 points at 7,874.90.
Traders said the bourse earlier resisted the slide on Wall Street due to strong industrial output figures released mid-morning.
